habit.lifeForm.basis: RHS plant record: "A large, vigorous evergreen climber". Bean: an evergreen climber "growing 20 to 30 ft high". Huang et al. 2024: a woody vine.

habit.stemLengthM.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "Stems to 6 m long".

habit.holdsBy.value: the stalks of its leaflets, which coil round a support
habit.holdsBy.basis: Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh: the stalk of each leaflet coils round a support that it touches and grips it. Bean: the secondary stalks are "1/2 to 1 in. long and twisted".

habit.bareBelow.value: the lower stems go bare after a few seasons
habit.bareBelow.basis: International Clematis Society (Rogerson, 1998): it puts its energy into growing upwards and will "leave its lower reaches bare after a few seasons".

stem.grooveCount.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "branches shallowly longitudinally 10-16-grooved".

stem.youngColour.basis: Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 18 April 2008: "The new vegetative shoots are a deep bronze red." International Clematis Society: "The youngest growth may be bronzy in both stem and leaf."

stem.oldDiameterMm.basis: Hong Kong Chinese Materia Medica Standards, Caulis Clematidis Armandii (the dried stem of this species): "long and cylindrical, slightly twisted, 1-5 cm in diameter".

stem.oldSurface.basis: Hong Kong Chinese Materia Medica Standards: "marked with longitudinal grooves and ridges. Nodes usually swollen, with leaf scars and branch scars. Any bark that remains is easily torn off."

stem.barkTexture.basis: Kwantlen Polytechnic University plant database, bark texture: exfoliating, stringy, moderately fissured.

stem.barkColour.basis: Kwantlen Polytechnic University plant database, bark colour: red to brown. The dried, stripped stem is "yellowish-brown or dull yellowish-brown" (Hong Kong Chinese Materia Medica Standards).

leaf.arrangement.basis: NC State Extension: leaves opposite. The Kwantlen plant database: compound, opposite.

leaf.division.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: leaves ternate. RHS: "trifoliate leaves".

leaf.leafletCount.basis: Bean (Trees and Shrubs Online): "Leaves composed of three leaflets". The same in every source read.

leaf.stalkLengthM.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "petiole 3.6-11 cm long". Bean: "the main-stalk is 1 1/2 to 4 in. long".

leaf.leafletStalkLengthM.basis: Bean: the stalks that carry the leaflets, "the secondary ones 1/2 to 1 in. long and twisted". In metres.

leaf.leafletLengthM.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "leaflet blades narrowly ovate, lanceolate, or ovate, 5-16 cm long, 1.5-7 cm broad". Bean: 3 to 6 in. long. RHS: "up to 15cm long".

leaf.leafletWidthM.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "5-16 cm long, 1.5-7 cm broad". Bean: 1 to 2 1/2 in. wide.

leaf.leafletShape.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "leaflet blades narrowly ovate, lanceolate, or ovate". Bean: "oblong-lanceolate to ovate".

leaf.leafletBase.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "base rounded, subcordate, or broadly cuneate". Bean: "rounded or slightly heart-shaped at the base".

leaf.leafletApex.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "apex acuminate to attenuate". Bean: "pointed".

leaf.margin.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "margin entire". Bean: "not toothed".

leaf.texture.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: leaflet blades leathery, glabrous on both surfaces. RHS: "leathery".

leaf.mainVeinCount.basis: Bean: the leaflets are "prominently three-veined". Huang et al. 2024: "basal veins abaxially prominent". The Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria count five veins from base to tip (https://hortflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/taxon/ad8c7fce-5340-11e7-b82b-005056b0018f): the outer pair is faint and is not drawn.

leaf.colour.basis: RHS plant record: "leathery, dark glossy green trifoliate leaves". Bean: "of a rich glossy green, and quite glabrous on both surfaces".

leaf.youngColour.basis: Clematis on the Web: the foliage is bronze when young. International Clematis Society: "The youngest growth may be bronzy in both stem and leaf."

leaf.posture.basis: Oregon State University, Landscape Plants: the leaflets droop. NC State Extension: droopy or cascading.

inflorescence.type.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "Cymes 1- to many-flowered, from axillary buds of old branches".

inflorescence.position.value: in the leaf axils of last year's shoots, a cluster to each axil
inflorescence.position.basis: International Clematis Society: the clusters are "usually paired along the stems and in bunches at the ends". Bean: "produced in April in dense axillary clusters". The leaves being opposite, a node has two axils.

inflorescence.flowersPerStalk.basis: Bean: flowers in dense axillary clusters, "mostly three on a stalk".

inflorescence.stalksPerAxil.basis: A dense cluster of flowers that stand three to a stalk has several stalks to an axil; no source read counts them. Two or three are drawn.

inflorescence.stalkLengthM.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "peduncle 0.4-8 cm long, puberulous or glabrous".

inflorescence.bractLengthM.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "bracts narrowly oblong to linear, 0.7-2 cm long".

inflorescence.budScaleLengthM.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "scales of axillary buds ovate, triangular, or oblong, 0.8-2 cm long". Bean: "The bases of the flower-stalks are surrounded by numerous bracts."

inflorescence.spanM.basis: The width of the two clusters of one node, from the outermost flower of one to the outermost of the other: what the growth model gives as organs.racemeLengthM and a flower record measures. This project's sum of the published stalk lengths and flower width, not a source's figure.

inflorescence.held.value: standing out from the leaf axils
inflorescence.held.basis: Cambridge University Botanic Garden: saucer-shaped flowers borne in axillary clusters, giving a mass of bloom. The growth model records the same as flowerHeld: facing_out.

flower.diameterM.basis: RHS plant record: "creamy-white flowers 5-6cm across". Bean: "Flowers 2 to 2 1/2 in. across". Huang et al. 2024 give 2 to 8 cm for the species over its whole range.

flower.stalkLengthM.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "Pedicel 1.8-7 cm long".

flower.sepalCount.basis: Bean: "sepals four to seven, narrow oblong". Huang et al. 2024: "Sepals 4 (-6)". There are no petals: the white parts are sepals.

flower.sepalCountUsual.basis: Garden plants most often have five or six: Clematis on the Web gives six as the commonest number for the garden form (var. biondiana) and four or five for the species; the Edinburgh plant had "6 petals"; Clemson Extension four, five or six. The mix drawn (mostly five and six, a few with four) is this project's.

flower.sepalLengthM.basis: Bean: sepals "about 1 in. long, 1/3 in. wide", in metres. Huang et al. 2024: 1.2 to 4.7 cm long.

flower.sepalWidthM.basis: Bean: sepals "about 1 in. long, 1/3 in. wide", in metres.

flower.sepalShape.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "Sepals 4 (-6), white or pinkish, spreading, narrowly oblong, obovate-oblong, or oblong". Bean: "narrow oblong".

flower.colour.basis: Bean: "pure or creamy white, changing to rose". RHS: "creamy-white". Huang et al. 2024: "white or pinkish".

flower.colourAged.basis: Bean: "pure or creamy white, changing to rose". Not drawn: the model's flower has one colour through its life.

flower.budColour.basis: Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh: the flowers "open pure white" from "globose silvery buds".

flower.stamenLengthM.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "Stamens 6-11 mm long, glabrous".

flower.antherLengthM.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "anthers narrowly oblong to linear, 3-4.5 mm long".

flower.antherColour.basis: Clematis on the Web: anthers cream or pale yellow. RHS: "with creamy stamens". The Edinburgh plant had "light coffee brown anthers", which is the colour after the pollen is shed.

flower.stamenCount.basis: Many (NC State Extension); a "central boss of stamens" (Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh). No source read counts them. Forty are drawn at the finest level of detail.

flower.styleLengthM.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "Style 6-8 mm long, densely villous".

fruit.type.value: head of achenes with feathered tails
fruit.type.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: achenes with a "persistent style 1.6-4.8 cm long, white plumose". NC State Extension: many small dry fruits, each with a silky, plumed tail.

fruit.acheneLengthM.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "Achenes narrowly ovate to elliptic-ovate, 4-5 mm long, 2-2.6 mm broad".

fruit.acheneWidthM.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "4-5 mm long, 2-2.6 mm broad".

fruit.tailLengthM.basis: Huang, Fei, Yuan & Yang (2024), Phytotaxa 670(4): 203-236, the description of Clematis armandi, read in the treatment deposited at Zenodo: "persistent style 1.6-4.8 cm long, white plumose".

fruit.colour.basis: Kwantlen Polytechnic University plant database: the fruit is white and feathery, in early summer.

fruit.achenesPerHead.basis: No source read counts the achenes of a head. Sixteen are drawn at the finest level of detail.

fruit.headsPerNode.basis: The seed heads that follow the flowers of one node. No source read says how many of a cluster's flowers ripen a head; a minority are drawn.

fruit.spanM.basis: The width of the seed heads of one node: what the growth model gives as fruit.lengthM and a fruit record measures. The heads stand on the stalks the flowers stood on, so the cluster is about as wide as the flowers were. This project's sum of the published tail and stalk lengths, not a source's figure.

hold.woundReachM.basis: The reach of a leaflet stalk where it is wound, from the node to the far side of the turn it makes round a support: the growth model's appendages.leafStalkLengthM. The thickness of a cable it can clasp (4 to 5 mm in the project's structures), the stalk's own thickness, and slack.

hold.turns.basis: A stalk is drawn making a turn and a quarter round what it holds. No source read says how many turns it makes; a stalk "1/2 to 1 in. long" (Bean) can make about one round a 5 mm cable.
